kind.editor: in the editor: its own list editor

text.layers:
Background layers (the page's "cover", a module's "slide.layers", "deck.backdrop").
ORDER = DEPTH: the first layer of the list lies deepest (at the very bottom), each next one lies ON the previous one, the last is on top — right under the slide's content. An opaque layer (a gradient, an image with "opacity" 1 or without transparency in the file) covers everything before it in the list. A large text ("bigtext") must therefore come AFTER an image if it should be visible on the image; an image with "blend": "multiply" needs a light layer before it in the list (underneath) or a light shared background (during a transition other than scrolling it blends only with its own slide's layers). The shared background ("deck.backdrop") lies under all layers of all slides; a slide's layers are visible only in its rectangle — they travel with it and vanish with it. In the editor the list is shown as on the screen: at the top what is on top (i.e. the reverse of the JSON).
Kinds, from those one usually starts with (deepest) to those on top:
  { "kind": "gradient", "speed": 0.12, "angle": 168, "from": "#12203a", "via": null, "to": "#060a12" }
  { "kind": "image", "speed": 0.34, "url": "https://…/tlo.jpg", "opacity": 0.45, "blend": "normal"|"multiply"|"screen"|"overlay"|"soft-light", "position": "center" }
  { "kind": "bigtext", "speed": 0.95, "lines": ["TRASA"], "opacity": 0.1, "color": null }
  { "kind": "glow", "speed": 0.12, "color": "rgba(120, 170, 220, 0.18)", "x": 58, "y": 42, "size": 60, "opacity": 1, "blend": "normal" } — glow: a soft patch of light; "x", "y" — centre in %, "size" — where it fades (% of the distance to the nearest edge)
  { "kind": "vignette", "speed": 0, "strength": 0.35, "reach": 55, "color": "#000000" } — dark corners: darker from "reach" % of the way to the corner, "strength" in the corner
  { "kind": "haze", "speed": 0.08, "color": "rgba(120, 170, 220, 0.08)", "depth": "rgba(30, 60, 100, 0.1)", "blur": 60, "opacity": 0.35, "motion": { "name": "drift" } } — haze: two dark patches ("depth") and a light streak ("color"), strongly blurred, drifting
  { "kind": "mesh", "speed": 0.05, "seed": 7, "count": 4, "color": "rgba(143, 208, 255, 0.25)", "glow": "rgba(167, 224, 255, 0.35)", "center": 0.82, "amplitude": 1, "opacity": 0.9, "dust": true, "motion": { "name": "sway" } } — threads: glowing wave lines above the bottom edge with dust; "count" layers, each waving its own way ("sway": 180–400 s); "center" — wave height (0 top, 1 bottom)
  { "kind": "waves", "speed": 0.05, "seed": 7, "count": 6, "hue": 188, "spread": 32, "opacity": 1, "blur": 1, "motion": [] } — waves: blurred bands near the bottom with light edges (hue "hue"…"hue"+"spread"); in the Cogita show they stand still — with "motion": { "name": "wave" } they flow
  "speed" 0–1 — how slowly the layer moves when scrolling; "opacity" 0–1. An image can be a page file: "page-image:<id>".
  Layer colours can be names: "ground", "accent", "ink", "muted" — then they follow the slides' colours. "seed" — the same number gives the same picture every time; "motion" — the layer's motion (below: Motion), "[]" — stands still.

A module's slide ("slide") — everything except "label" and "layers" is optional:
  "transition" — how this slide replaces the previous one: "scroll" (comes in from below, the default), "flow" (flow: the content moves up with the scrolling and blends at the same time — the previous one moves up and fades with its layers, this one comes in from below and appears; the layers move slower than the content, each at its own pace), "fade" (crossfades in place: the content stands; when the new slide is transparent, the previous one fades meanwhile), "cover" (covers the previous one, which dims), "reveal" (the previous one moves away and reveals it), "zoom" (zoom), "side" (from the right), "dissolve" (dissolve: the previous one fades, blurs and sinks by 12 px, this one sharpens while rising — like the Cogita show). It follows the scrolling, not a clock
  "enter" — how the content appears: "none", "rise", "fade", "zoom", "left", "right"
  "colors" — the slide's own colours, changing smoothly between slides: { "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted" } ("#rrggbb"; left out — like the page)
  "stage" — the module has NO slide of its own: it stands above all and, when the slide changes, moves to its place on the next one:
      { "frames": { "<id of the module-slide or "cover">": { "x": 50, "y": 50, "w": 30, "scale": 1, "rotate": 0, "opacity": 1 } }, "bare": false }
      "x", "y" — centre in percent of the stage; "w" — width in percent; between slides with a place it moves smoothly, before the first and after the last it stands; "bare": true — without a frame (logo, image)
      "max" — at most this width in rem (a logo stays a logo on a large screen); "tall" — other values on a screen taller than wide (phone): { "x", "y", "w", "scale", "rotate", "opacity" } — only those that differ; with its own "w" on a phone exactly that counts
  "motion" — the module's motion on its slide or on the stage (below: Motion), e.g. { "name": "rise", "delay": 220 } — the text rises once the slide is reached
  "layout" — where the slide's content stands: { "align": "start"|"center"|"end", "valign": "start"|"center"|"end", "width": 68, "tall": { "align", "valign", "width" } } — "width" in percent of the stage (stage width — "deck.width"); "tall" — on a phone; left out — in the centre, a comfortable text width
  "with" — the module has NO slide of its own: it stands beside another on its slide, in one row: { "slide": "<module id>", "side": "end"|"start", "share": 42, "tallSide": "start"|"end" } — "side" on the right / on the left, "share" — % of the row width, "tallSide" — on a phone above / below it (an image, an animation beside a text); "with": "<id>" is enough too
text.presentation:
Scenes are screens; modules stand on them anywhere. A scene can have several steps — then the highlight moves from module to module, and the scene follows the highlighted one. A module with a place on several scenes travels: when the scene changes it moves smoothly to its next place. Everything follows the scrolling (wheel, finger, arrows), in the “Show” — the keyboard and clicks.
Inside a scene a module can change with its PROGRESS ("frames" of a place): a large photo shrinks to a frame, moves, is revealed through a mask — scrolling back undoes the change, stopping stops it, and wheel, finger, keyboard and show move the same progress. The more "steps" a scene has, the longer its way.
Scenes don't have to go in order: each has one entrance and exits — “next” (arrows, scrolling: "next") and buttons (modules with "go"). An exit leads to a scene, to the end ("end") or outside ("link:<id>" from "links"). Whoever presses a button goes on that way; back — the way they came.

The page's "show":
  "format" — "screen" (full screen, like a home page; on a phone upright — with "tall" places), "wide" (16:9), "classic" (4:3)
  "fonts" — typeface: "app", "spectral" (Spectral + IBM Plex Sans), "cormorant" (Cormorant Garamond + Source Sans), "plex" (IBM Plex Sans)
  "nav" — the scene bar: "labels" (names at the top), "dots" (dots on the right), "none"
  "links" — ways out: [{ "id": "zapisy", "label": "Zapisz się", "href": "https://…" | "#/strona" | "mailto:…" }] — the exit of a scene or a button leads there through "link:<id>"
  "width" — at most this many rem of stage width: the module places count within it (x, y in percent), the background stays on the whole screen (e.g. 80 — like the Cogita show); left out — the whole window
  "sound" — ambient sound (fire, leaves), only at the viewer's request: { "url": "page-image:<id>" | "https://…/ogrod.mp3", "label": "Odgłosy ogrodu", "volume": 0.6 } — the bottom bar has a button with "label"; nothing plays without a click; it loops, goes quiet when the tab is hidden. File: MP3, M4A, OGG or WAV (a page file up to 30 MB). Volume on a scene — the scene's "volume"
  "backdrop" — shared background: layers (as for slides: "gradient", "image", "glow", "vignette", "haze", "mesh", "waves" …) standing behind all scenes; scenes are then transparent, and their own background (colour "ground", layers "layers") lies in it and changes smoothly into the next one's
  "map" — where the scenes stand on the transition map in the editor: { "<scene key>" | "link:<id>" | "gate:{keyTag}" | "end": { "x", "y" } } — for the editor only
  "story" — a RUN (as in Cogita): questions, conditions, values; a presentation with the "question" module always has one (then the answers stay in the browser). { "base": "<knowledge base id>", "storage": "<area id>", "values": [...], "gates": [...] }
    "base" — the knowledge base (Cogita) in which the answers of signed-in people (and people from a form) count; left out — an example: answers, values and the place where someone stopped stay only in the browser
    "storage" — the area (with intake) the answers go to; left out — the person's private area
    "values" — [{ "id": "pkt", "label": "Punkty", "start": 0, "min": 0, "max": 10 }] — values of the run (points, closeness to a character)
    in the knowledge base the same run is the run {"look": "scenes", "presentation": "<address of this page>"} (Presentation → Transitions → “Run in Learning”): in Learning it plays this presentation, answers and place count in the base — without a copy
    "gates" — gates between scenes; the exit of a scene, a button or a question leads to a gate through "gate:{keyTag}":
      { "key": "czy-umie", "label": "Umie?", "type": "condition", "when": { "type": "answered", "of": "<question module id>", "correct": true }, "yes": "<scene key>", "no": "<scene key>" } — a condition (as in Cogita: "answered", "value" { "value": "pkt", "op": "ge", "than": 3 }, "visited" { "of": "<scene key>" }, "knowness", "time", "and"/"or"/"not" with "items")
      { "key": "punkt", "type": "set", "actions": [{ "type": "add", "value": "pkt", "by": 1 } | { "type": "set", "value": "pkt", "to": 0 }], "next": "{targetTag}" } — changes values, then leads on
  "scenes" — the list of scenes in order:
    "key" — the scene key (short, unique, e.g. "start"); module places point to a scene by its key
    "label" — the name in the bar; a link "#name" in a text leads to this scene
    "steps" — how many steps (stops) the scene has; by default 1
    "change" — how it replaces the previous one: "fade" (crossfade), "build" (the scene is there at once, its modules arrive each their own way — "arrive"), "fly" (the camera flies through the PREVIOUS scene — its modules with depth and the word cloud), "rise", "zoom", "cover", "reveal", "side", "cut", "dissolve" (dissolve: the previous one fades, blurs and sinks by 12 px, this one sharpens while rising — like the Cogita show)
    "keep" — true: the previous scene stays underneath until the transition ends (with "fade", "build", "rise")
    "duration" — how long the jump to this scene takes in ms (by default 700, with "fly" 1700)
    "colors" — { "accent", "ink", "ground" (scene background), "muted" } — left out: like the whole presentation
    "layers" — background layers (as for slides, without moving)
    "grow" — { "from": 0.8, "to": 1.08 } — the scene grows from the entrance to the last step
    "follow" — { "wide": 0.45, "tall": 1 } — how strongly the scene moves so that the highlighted module stands in the middle (wide / narrow screen)
    "emphasis" — false: steps don't highlight modules (by default true: the non-highlighted ones fade and move away from the middle)
    "thread" — a thread through the modules with steps, in step order: "none", "line", "dots"
    "hint" — a small hint at the bottom (e.g. "Scroll"); it disappears when you move on
    "words" — a word cloud in the depth: { "list": ["colligere", …], "prefix": "RE", "count": 39, "seed": 7, "color": null }
    "depth" — { "perspective": 1000, "travel": 2200, "linger": true } — the scene's depth and how far the camera flies; "linger" — slows down at the deepest module
    "next" — where “next” leads (arrows, scrolling): a scene key, "end" (the end here) or "link:<id>"; left out — the next scene on the list
    "about" — in a story with a knowledge base ("story.base"): what the scene is about — entries of that base, ["@kurs/temat"] (id or @name); the story's path (module "path", Learning) places the scene next to them — so the introduction and the place where the ways meet stand on the map too, though they have no question (questions add what they are about themselves)
    "volume" — how loud the ambient sound ("sound") is on this scene, 0–1 (left out — 1; 0 — silence); it changes smoothly between scenes

A module's "show":
  "places" — { "<scene key>": place } — one place: the module belongs to that scene; several: it travels
    place: { "x": 50, "y": 50, "w": 30, "h": null, "max": null, "rotate": 0, "scale": 1, "opacity": 1, "z": 0, "step": null, "tall": null }
      "x", "y" — the module's point (usually the centre — see "origin") in percent of the scene; "w" — width in percent of the width; "h" — height in percent of the height (null — like the content)
      "max" — at most this width in rem (e.g. 22): on a large screen the module doesn't grow further, on a phone it takes "w" percent
      "z" — depth in pixels (0 flat, −980 far away); "step" — in which step of the scene it is highlighted (from 0)
      "tall" — other values on a narrow screen: { "x", "y", "w", "h", "max", "scale", "rotate", "crop", "mask" } (only those that differ)
      "crop" — the crop point of the image at this place: "57% 40%", "center", "left top" — with cropping ("fit": "cover" of the "image" module, an image in the "media" frame) this point stays in view when the field changes size (the focus stays the focus, on a phone too — "crop" in "tall"); left out — the image's "at"; it changes smoothly in frames
      "mask" — what of the module is visible: a circle { "shape": "circle", "r": 40, "x": 50, "y": 50 } ("r" — radius in %; 71 reaches the corners when the centre is in the middle), an oval { "shape": "ellipse", "rx": 60, "ry": 40, "x": 50, "y": 50 } ("rx" — % of the width, "ry" — % of the height), a rectangle { "shape": "inset", "top": 10, "right": 10, "bottom": 10, "left": 10, "round": 1.5 } (insets in %, "round" — corners in rem); null — the whole module; in frames masks of the same shape change smoothly, and a mask from null grows from the whole
      "frames" — FRAMES driven by the scene's progress (not a clock), at most 16: [{ "at": 0.4, "x": 30, "w": 40, "h": 55, "crop": "50% 60%" }, …] — "at" 0–1 of the progress or "step": the scene's step number (from 0) instead of "at"; a frame changes only what it gives ("x", "y", "w", "h", "max", "rotate", "scale", "opacity", "z", "crop", "mask"), the rest stays as in the frame before it; the place itself is the state at 0; the module moves smoothly to each frame with its "ease" ("inOut" — usual, "linear", "in", "out"); after the last one it stays; a frame without changes holds the state (e.g. { "at": 0.3 } — stands until 0.3); "tall" in a frame — its other values on a phone
      "by" — what the frames' progress is: "scene" (usual) — the inside of the scene: 0 at the first step, 1 at the last (the scene must have at least 2 "steps"; with 1 step it stands at 0); "enter" — the scene's entrance: 0 when the transition from the previous one starts, 1 when the scene is there; "leave" — the scene's exit: 0 at the last step, 1 when the next one is already there
      "still" — with “reduce motion”: at which progress (0–1) the frames stand — a still composition with the same headings, images and buttons; left out — at the end (with "leave" — at the beginning), and frames with "step" then jump from step to step, without the way between
  "skin" — the frame: "plain" (no background), "card" (a panel), "bubble" (a bubble), "pill" (a pill), "panel" (a field filling "w"×"h")
  "type" — only "text": "auto" (as on the page), "display" (a huge sentence — the page heading), "title" (capitals), "heading" (a heading with content), "kicker" (a heading in the accent colour with content), "body" (paragraphs), "close" (the punchline: italics in the accent colour, an empty line separates groups), "note" (a small note)
  "fill", "ink", "accent" — background, text and accent colour (links, punchline): "#rrggbb", a pair "light|dark" or a name: "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted"
  "origin" — which point of the module stands on "x", "y": "center" (default), "top-left", "top", "top-right", "left", "right", "bottom-left", "bottom", "bottom-right"
  "media" — an image in the frame: { "url", "at": "57% 50%", "fit": "cover"|"contain", "size": 60, "max": null, "opacity": 1, "fade": true, "side": "after"|"before"|"behind" } — with "contain": "size" in percent of the place, "max" at most this many rem
  "align", "valign" — "start", "center", "end"
  "arrive" — how it appears: "none", "fade", "rise", "zoom", "grow", "left", "right", "from-left", "from-right", "from-top", "from-bottom" (with "from-…" it comes in from beyond the edge)
  "delay", "span" — when in the transition it starts (0–1) and what part of it it lasts (0–1)
  "ease" — the travelling module's motion: "inOut", "linear", "in" (accelerates), "out"
  "hold" — true: it also stands before its first and after its last place
  "between" — a module with places on scenes NOT in a row: "glide" — glides through the scenes in between (usual), "leave" — leaves with its scene and comes back with the next one where it has a place (the same image at the beginning and at the end of a story, and not in the middle); it then always stands in the scene it is on — like its own module
  "layer" — higher is in front; a travelling one with a negative value (-1 … -5) stands in front of the scene background but behind its texts (a photo over the whole scene, and a caption on it) — in the scene of its first place, with "between": "leave" in the scene it is just on; a travelling one from 10 stands above all scenes
  "go" — the module is a button: { "<scene key>": target } — on this scene a click leads to the target (a scene key, "end", "link:<id>", "step" — to this module's own step on this scene: highlights it, the scene stays, "step:2" — to step 3 of this scene; "" — nowhere yet); instead of a scene key "*" — on every scene the module stands on (e.g. a fixed button “Contact” with "hold": true), a scene key takes precedence over "*"; a question ("question") has result exits instead: { "<scene key>:right": target, "<scene key>:wrong": target } — where “Next” leads after a right and after a wrong answer (left out — the scene's “next”); the target can also be a gate "gate:{keyTag}"
  "motion" — motion by the clock (description: Motion): once, when the scene is reached (e.g. { "name": "rise", "delay": 220 } — the text rises on arrival), or in a loop, as long as the module is visible; independent of "arrive", which follows the scrolling; with "by" ("scene", "enter", "leave") the motion follows the scene's progress instead of the clock — e.g. { "name": "keys", "by": "enter", "keys": [{ "at": 0, "clip": "circle(0% at 50% 50%)" }, { "at": 1, "clip": "circle(75% at 50% 50%)" }] } — the photo is revealed through a growing circle as the scene enters

Text ("text") in a presentation and on a page: "## " — a subheading, "# " — a large line, "> " — a small, quiet line, [caption](https://… | #/strona | #scena | mailto:… | tel:…) — a link; a line of only links is a row of links.
text.appointments:
A page can bring appointments (a retreat, a pilgrimage, a festival) together with their programme. The import ADDS them to calendars — each import anew (two imports are the same appointments twice). Appointments already in a calendar are shown by the page with a module through their id, not through "appointments".
Entrances ("calendars"): each entrance is a place the appointments go to; on import the importing person chooses for each entrance one of their calendars they can write in (like the area for the answers to a form's new questions).
  entrance: { "key": a short name (letters, digits, - and _), "label": how the importing person will see it, "calendar": calendar id — only a suggestion }
  An appointment without "calendar" goes to the entrance "{entry}"; an entrance without a description in "calendars" works too (its name is its "key").
Appointment (an entry in "appointments"):
  "key" — a short name by which modules point to this appointment: "@name" (e.g. "item" of the "program" module)
  "calendar" — the entrance (= "key" from "calendars"); programme points go to the calendar of their appointment
  "title" — the appointment's name (required)
  "start" — "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" (local time) or "YYYY-MM-DD" (all day); in a programme point "HH:MM" is enough (the day of its appointment), and without "start" a point starts together with its appointment
  "end" — the same; "HH:MM" is the same day; for all day — the last day (inclusive); without "end": an hour, for all day — one day
  "allDay" — true: all day (also when "start" has a time)
  "location", "notes" — place and description
  "link", "linkLabel" — “More information”: an address https://… or #/path and the text on the button
  "repeat" — only an appointment (not a point): "none", "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "yearly"; "every" — every how many (1–99); "weekdays" — with "weekly": ["pn", "wt", "śr", "cz", "pt", "so", "nd"] (without them — the day of "start"); "until" — "YYYY-MM-DD" the last day (without it — no end)
  "points" — programme points: a list of appointments (the same keys, without "calendar" and "repeat"), also with their own "points" — at most {depth} levels; at most {max} appointments together with points
Modules point to appointments and entrances through "@name": "program" — "item": "@appointment name" (an empty "calendar" gets this appointment's calendar by itself, or "calendar": "@entrance"); "calendar" — "calendars": "@entrance" (also next to ids, separated by commas). After the import real ids stand there.

text.images:
A page can ask for files that don't exist yet — photos, a short video, a sound, a document to download. Describe each in "images", and where it should stand write "{prefix}key" instead of "page-image:<id>" — in a module, in a background layer, in a presentation scene, in the menu, wherever an image or file address stands. Before the import the importing person adds a file to each description (or chooses a file the page already has); the import uploads them to the page's files (public like the page) and puts them in every place with "{prefix}key".
File description (an entry in "images"):
  "key" — a short name (letters, digits, - and _), the same as in "{prefix}key"
  "label" — a short title the importing person will see (without it — "key")
  "description" — what the file should show: subject, framing, time of day, mood, landscape or portrait and what it will serve for — the importing person chooses the file by it
  "name" — the file name, if known (e.g. "IMG_3240.jpg"): files with this name are assigned by themselves, also those the page already has
  "kind" — "image" (usual: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF, up to 8 MB), "video" (MP4 or WebM, up to 30 MB), "sound" (MP3, M4A, OGG or WAV, up to 30 MB) or "file" (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, GPX or an image, up to 25 MB)
A description nobody added a file to: its places stay empty (a module without an image) — the import says so, and you add the file later in the editor. "{prefix}key" without a description in "images" works too — the importing person gets it without a description. At most {max} files.

text.intro:
What the import does:
- The document describes the whole page: title, text, look (a page with modules or slides), colours, menu, logic map and modules — each with its content. A key not in the document stays unchanged on the page.
- Export → change → import changes the page IN PLACE: a module with an "id" from the export stays the same module (with its registrations, people's links and place in the logic map). A module without "id" is created new.
- “Replace the page's modules”: the page's modules become exactly those from the document, the others disappear from the page. Without it the modules from the document are changed or added, and the rest stays.
- The import saves at once. An export before the import is a backup.
- An event document from the old system ({ "title", "pages": [{ "parts": [...] }] }) and a single module ("{module}") are accepted too — the latter is added to the page.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.
text.keys:
"format" — "{format}"
  "version" — 1
  "path" — information only; the import always goes to the open page
  "title" — the page title
  "lead" — the text under the title (or null)
  "mode" — "page": modules on a grid; "slides": each module is a separate slide; "presentation": scenes with modules anywhere (below: Presentation)
  "lang" — the page language: "en", "de" or "pl" — every visitor sees the app's texts on this page in this language; left out or null — everyone in their own language (the content is written by the author and not translated)
  "theme" — colours: null (automatic — as in the app) or { "mode": "dark"|"light", "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted" } (colours "#rrggbb"); with "night": { "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted" } the page follows the device — light colours by day, these at night
  "cover" — the title slide background: a list of layers (below)
  "show" — presentation scenes (below: Presentation)
  "deck" — the slide show as a whole (only "mode": "slides"): { "backdrop": [layers], "nav": "labels"|"dots"|"none", "titleSlide": true|false, "width": 80 }
      "backdrop" — shared background: layers (as below) that stand behind all slides and lie UNDER their own layers — so the shared background's gradient doesn't cover the slides' images; the slides move over it transparent, and their own layers travel with their slide (in its rectangle): in a transition they move up with it, fade or get covered like it — nothing of the previous slide stays on the next one; a slide without its own layers is transparent (the shared background shows through)
      "nav" — the bar: slide names at the top (usual), dots on the right, no bar; "titleSlide": false — no title slide (the first module is the first screen)
      "width" — at most this many rem of stage width: the places of modules moving between slides and the slides' "layout" count within it (null — the whole window)
  "menu" — null (no menu), a list of items or { "from": "path" } (the same menu as on another of your pages)
      item: { "label", "kind": "abs" (path from the root, e.g. "parafia/zapisy") | "rel" (relative to this page) | "url" (full address) | "none" (heading only), "target", "children": [items], "image" }
      "image" — an image instead of the name (logo): "page-image:<id>" (an image of this page), "https://…" or "/logo.svg"; "label" stays — a screen reader reads it and it shows when the image is missing
  "subject" — choice on the page: at the top of the page one thing is chosen, and modules (e.g. "entry-panel") show it. {subject}
  "logic" — the page's logic map (when which module is visible, the person's steps) or null. It's easiest to build it in the editor; in JSON: { "version": 1, "nodes": [...], "edges": [...] }
      node: { "id", "kind", "x", "y", ... } — kind: {nodes}
      "part" has "partId" (= the module's "id") and "message"; "step" has "label", "help", "dueAt" (YYYY-MM-DD), "goto" (= the module's "id");
      "registered"/"confirmed"/"answer"/"mark" have "formId"; "answer" — "fieldId", "op" ("filled"|"empty"|"eq"|"ne"), "valueHash"; "mark" — "stepId", "markBy" ("office"|"person"); "date" — "when" ("after"|"before"), "date"
      edge: { "id", "from", "to", "port": "show"|"done"|"applies"|"in" }
  "modules" — modules in reading order
  "appointments" — appointments for the calendar, with a programme (points and sub-points): the import ADDS them to calendars the importing person chooses (below: Appointments for the calendar); the export doesn't contain them
  "calendars" — entrances for appointments: which calendars they should go to (the importing person chooses a calendar for each entrance)
  "images" — files the page needs that don't exist yet (photos, a video, a sound, a document), each with a description: the importing person adds them before the import, and the import puts them everywhere "{prefix}key" stands (below: Files to add); the export doesn't contain them
text.texts: A short text (a greeting, an announcement, a few sentences) stays in the module — e.g. "text". A longer text (a sermon, a conference, a meditation, a chapter) lives in the Scriptorium and is shown from there: the module "writing" (one text — with a plan, deliveries, footnotes) or "writings" (an archive of one scriptorium's texts). Then a correction in the Scriptorium is at once on every page, and the scriptorium's area decides who sees the text. Quotes are shown by the module "quotes" (from the Library).
text.usage:
- The page stands at recreatio.pl/#/<page path> (also under an alias or an own domain pointing to it) — as a grid of modules, slides or a presentation ("mode").
- The menu ("menu") stands on this page and on pages that take it through { "from" }; subpages don't inherit it.
- Modules read data live: calendars ("calendar", "program"), forms, Scriptorium texts, Library quotes, knowledge bases, the area's conversation ("chat"). Everyone sees as much of them as they themselves can read.
- A module standing on several pages is one: changed content changes on each of them. A module taken off the page (also through “Replace the page's modules”) disappears only from it — a form with questions or registrations stays in “Modules”.
- A personal link from a form opens the page on which the person's modules (“Person's registration”, “Person's steps”…) show their registration, steps and conversations. The logic map ("logic") only hides modules in the browser — it is not a protection.
- A module of a public page can be embedded on another site as a widget (“Embed on another site” in the editor); the widget won't show a page with access.
- A public page is seen by everyone, without an account. It saves only when an area with a data controller responsible for it is named (“Who is responsible for this page” in the editor); the page footer says who is responsible for the content and has “Report content”.
- A page with access is seen by the people of its areas (account, link, personal link) and those who run it. The server also knows its content — unless the page is encrypted (Address tree → Settings).
- The page's files (photos, videos, documents) are not encrypted: whoever knows a file's address will open it — also from a page with access.
- The page title is visible in “Your pages” of those who run it or have access to it; the cards “Events” and “Business card” lead to the area's main page (without a business card they take its title and text); a knowledge base run in Learning can play the presentation.
- The page document doesn't change its address, access, encryption or the area responsible for it (the access of an area's pages is set by "access" in the area document).
- The preview before the import (preview.html; for AI assistants — the MCP server recreatio-preview) draws the page the way the import will make it, and saves nothing.

entry.id: The module's place on this page. From the export — the module is changed in place (registrations, links, logic map stay). Left out or unknown — a new place is created
entry.module: The module this place shows (the same module can stand on several pages). For a new place left out — a new module is created; for a place with "id" — the current one stays
entry.name: The module's name in the module list (optional)
entry.lang: The module's language: "en", "de" or "pl" — the app's texts in the module (buttons, hints) are in this language. Left out or null — the page's language
entry.slide: How it looks as a slide: { "label": name in the slide menu (the anchor "#name" comes from it), "layers": [background layers], "transition", "enter", "colors", "stage" } — details below (A module's slide)
entry.show: Where it stands in the presentation ("mode": "presentation"): { "places": { "<scene key>": place }, "skin", "type", … } — details below (Presentation). null — takes the module off the presentation
entry.size: Size when you don't give "layout": { "colSpan": 2|3|4|6, "rowSpan": 1|3|5 } — 1 strip, 3 block, 5 tall. Place: the first free one
entry.layout: The exact place on the grid for "desktop" (6 columns), "tablet" (4) and "mobile" (2): { "position": { "row", "col" }, "size": { "colSpan", "rowSpan" } }. Left out — the module stays where it was (a new one: the first free place)
entry.config: The module's content — depends on the kind (below). Left out — the content stays unchanged
entry.needs: Only "form": requirements — minors, health, insurance, rules (below: Form requirements). Also "memberRoles", "virtualAreas", "group", "repeat", "audience" — everything a module document carries (below: Form)

node.kindsText: The content ("config") depends on the kind of module ("kind"): each kind has its own keys and an example.
node.usage: How the app uses this data
node.layers: Background layers and a module's slide

part.title: Content of the module “{name}” as JSON
part.unknown: The kind “{kind}” is not known to this version.
part.text: What the import does here: the content ("config") replaces the current content of this module in the page draft — “Save modules” saves it. It accepts the "config" object alone, an entry { "kind", "config" } or a whole entry from a page export (its "config" counts). Keys you don't give stay empty.

module.title: Module as JSON ("{format}", version 1)
module.intro: What the import does here: it changes THIS module — its name and content — on all pages it stands on. A key not in the document stays unchanged. The import saves at once.
module.introForm: What the import does here: it changes THIS module — its name and content — on all pages it stands on. In addition what belongs to the form: questions, layout, requirements, roles and person areas (below: Form). A key not in the document stays unchanged. The import saves at once.
module.keys:
"format" — "{format}"
  "version" — 1
  "id" — module id (information only — the import always changes the open module)
  "kind" — kind; must match the open module
  "name" — the name in the module list
  "config" — content, depending on the kind (below)
module.unknown: The kind “{kind}” is not known to this version — "config" passes unchanged.
